tests.name: Clean committed shipped-composition deterministic repeats
observed: Each iteration ran the base Link session slice, the two-controller settlement scenario, and the dispatch-barrier closure regression.
Each settlement scenario ran Controller A first and Controller B first, for six controlled approval rounds across the clean repeats.
The winner and the already admitted loser both received HTTP 200 with an exact void result of {ok:true} and no value field.
The losing Controller received exactly one cancel; a third late result was refused with forbidden/interaction.
Both Client generations ended without a pending interaction, and each round appended exactly one matching approval/asked and approval/decided pair.
The barrier regression covered releaseAll-before-late-arrival, a pre-aborted arrival, and abort while an arrival was waiting.

acceptance: The test boots the shipped base plus desktop Loader composition and drives the real TLS Link carrier.
Controller A and Controller B pair through /link/pair; the Observer is registered through the shipped Device Trust owner because pairingRole is deployment-fixed.
All three participants open authenticated persistent $events streams with Host-issued clientId values, while only the Controllers receive the pending approval.
The Host dispatch barrier observes both signed answers after Link has claimed each generation and before Gateway settlement, then releases A first and B first in separate rounds.
The admitted loser converges through an idempotent void success and exactly one cancel; a new late submission is refused by the now-absent interaction.
Gateway pending state is false for both Controllers after settlement, and the real Session contains one durable approval decision for each request.
Failure cleanup permanently opens the barrier, restores the Gateway method to close new wrapped ingress, aborts and joins requests, and drains every dispatch already owned by the wrapper.
The suite isolates DSH_HOME, awaits stream closure and Cordis disposal, restores the prior environment, and aggregates independent cleanup failures.
knownLimitations: This Host-side E4 acceptance does not execute Swift or Kotlin clients; cross-language execution remains owned by G1-E2E.

The deterministic barrier intentionally spies on the private TypertGatewayService.dispatchRpc method. A Gateway refactor will fail the Host typecheck or the acceptance loudly and requires moving the test hook to the new pre-settlement owner.
